title: EvoX: active mechanism selection and reuse
summary: EvoX joins the GAx search/mode line with AnotherOddThing's active-identification idea. Its early gates test whether evolution can retain distinct executable procedures and later identify/reuse the right one; V3 extracts the successful half into a domain-agnostic Bayesian intervention engine and tests the same core across regression faults, state machines, program transforms, noisy dynamics and a causal circuit. Four of five frozen canonical domains pass; the causal-circuit adapter improves over random but misses the predeclared identification-efficiency margin.

nodes.claim: Given several executable explanations that fit current observations, choose interventions by expected information gain, update belief over mechanisms, and reuse the identified mechanism instead of restarting search.
nodes.survived: The active-identification/reuse mechanism generalized beyond the original direct-versus-relational toy world. On frozen V3 canonical seeds, the same domain-agnostic engine passed 4/5 adapters: regression faults, state machines, program transforms and noisy dynamics; once the useful mechanism was identified, reuse was consistently cheaper than restart.
nodes.killed: The broader story remains bounded. Earlier V0-V2 work did not make alternative procedures reliably abundant, and V3 is not a universal cross-domain PASS: the causal-circuit adapter still benefited from active probing but missed the frozen identification-efficiency threshold, so the overall 5/5 gate failed.

edges.why: EvoX explicitly starts from GAx's question of retaining and separating alternative computational procedures, then tests whether those alternatives can be identified and reused under a new context.
EvoX explicitly imports AnotherOddThing's active experimental-design mechanism: choose the intervention that maximally separates currently plausible hidden mechanisms under a bounded probe budget.
